label: Big kid toilet

what_happens.title: How the big kid toilet works
goals: The body gives a feeling when wee or poo is coming
Wee and poo go in the potty or toilet
Learning takes time, and accidents happen
what_happens.parentSkill: Use simple, calm words for wee and poo and read a short book about potties together.

who_is_there.title: Who helps me
goals: Teachers and carers help with toilets too
Other kids are learning as well
who_is_there.parentSkill: Stay close and calm; let your child choose whether you stay in the bathroom or wait at the door.

what_i_do.title: What I do on the toilet
goals: Listen to the tummy feeling and go straight away
what_i_do.parentSkill: Make a picture chart of the toilet steps and stick it next to the potty.

if_scared.title: If it feels hard
goals: Accidents happen to everyone who is learning
The flush is loud, and nobody has to flush
Calm tools: slow breaths, a song, trying again later
if_scared.parentSkill: After an accident say: 'That's okay, bodies are learning. Let's clean up together.'

rehearsal.title: Let's practise the toilet steps
goals: Practise with a doll or a toy on the potty
Say the steps: feel, tell, sit, wipe, wash
rehearsal.parentSkill: Let a toy have a turn on the potty first and praise the toy for trying.

steps: Notice the wee or poo feeling in the tummy
Tell a grown-up, I need the toilet
Pull pants down and sit on the potty or the toilet seat
Wait and let the wee or poo come out
Wipe with toilet paper, a grown-up helps
Pull pants up and flush, or tip the potty with help
Wash hands with soap and water
sensory: the loud whoosh of the flush
a tummy feeling that says it is time
warm soapy water on the hands
a little step stool under the feet
honestyNotes: Accidents are normal and part of learning; never shame, punish or call them naughty. The flush is loud and can be scary; the child never has to flush. Bodies work in their own time; never promise it will be easy or quick. Use the family's own words for wee and poo.

fallbackAnswer: No. A potty is small and low, and a big toilet can have a little seat on top.
[[GROWNUP]] can hold you while you sit.

questionButtons.text: Why is the flush so loud?
fallbackAnswer: The flush is water rushing away, whoosh, and it is loud.
You do not have to flush, and you can cover your ears.

questionButtons.text: What if I have an accident?
fallbackAnswer: Accidents happen to everyone who is learning. It is okay.
We clean up together and try again next time.
It goes down the pipes, far away, to a place that cleans the water.
It does not come back.
Usually not, and soft poos come out easily.
If it feels sore, tell [[GROWNUP]], and drinking water and eating fruit can help.
[[GROWNUP]] helps you, or your teacher at daycare.
You will learn to do it yourself, little by little.

questionButtons.text: Can I use the toilet at daycare?
fallbackAnswer: Yes. Teachers help kids with toilets every day.
You can say, I need the toilet, please.

questionButtons.text: Do I still wear a diaper at night?
fallbackAnswer: Many kids still wear night pants for a while, and that is normal.
Night dryness comes later for lots of kids.

questionButtons.text: What if I need to go when we are out?
fallbackAnswer: Shops, parks and restaurants have toilets.
Tell [[GROWNUP]] quickly, and we will find one together.

questionButtons.text: Why do I have to wait so long?
fallbackAnswer: Sometimes the body needs a few minutes to relax.
A book or a song makes the waiting easier.

techniques.label: Picture steps chart
techniques.how: Stick a picture chart of the toilet steps beside the potty.

techniques.label: A little step stool
techniques.how: Use a stool so feet rest flat and the body feels steady.

techniques.label: Blowing slow bubbles
techniques.how: Blow slow pretend bubbles to help the body relax.

techniques.label: Flush is optional
techniques.how: Let your child leave before you flush, or cover the ears.

techniques.label: Try times
techniques.how: Sit on the potty after meals and before bath, when bodies are most ready.

techniques.label: A spare clothes kit
techniques.how: Pack spare pants and wipes so accidents are no big deal.

techniques.label: Teaching a toy
techniques.how: Let your child teach a toy the steps.

techniques.label: Asking the teacher
techniques.how: Practise the sentence, I need the toilet, please, for daycare.

techniques.label: Smell the flower, blow the candle
techniques.how: Breathe in slowly through the nose and out like blowing a candle.

ritual: Feel the tummy, tell a grown-up
Wash hands and a happy dance

pain: If it feels sore, tell me. Water and fruit help.
Take a slow breath and let your body relax.
body: Your body is learning, a little every day.
sensory: The flush is loud. You can leave first.
The seat can feel cold for a moment.
strangers: Teachers help kids with toilets every day.
You can say, I need the toilet, please.
separation: I'm right here. I can stay or wait by the door.
unknown: First sit, then wait a little.
safety: You will not fall in. I can hold you.
social: Lots of kids are learning right now.
Big kids learned too, step by step.
love: Accidents are okay. I love you.
I'm proud of you for trying.

Learning to use the toilet is a skill, like learning to ride a bike, and every body learns at its own speed.
The brain and the bladder have to learn to talk to each other, and that takes practice.
Some kids are dry in the day long before they are dry at night, and that is normal.
Drinking water and eating fruit helps poos come out easily.
[[CHILD]] can sit on the toilet after meals, when the body is most ready.
Teachers, carers and doctors all know that toilet learning is a normal part of growing up.
If accidents keep happening at night, a doctor can explain why, and it is never a child's fault.
Lots of kids still wear night pants for years, and nobody needs to know.
Family members can share their own stories of learning.
[[CHILD]] can choose a private word to tell [[GROWNUP]] quietly.
Taking time on the toilet helps the body empty properly.
Feet flat on a stool help the tummy muscles relax, which is why many families use one.
Holding wee in for a long time can make accidents more likely.
Wiping front to back keeps the body clean and healthy.
[[CHILD]] can set a reminder to try the toilet before leaving the house.
Accidents are normal for months, and stress, illness or changes like a new sibling can bring them back for a while.
If poos feel hard or sore, that is constipation, and a doctor can help with simple changes.
Feeling embarrassed is common, and nobody needs to know apart from the family.
Night dryness depends on a hormone that develops in its own time.
[[CHILD]] can pack spare clothes in a bag, so an accident is no big deal.
A simple chart with stickers can track tries, not just successes.
Practising at set times, like after breakfast and before bath, builds a habit.
It helps to know where the toilets are when going out.
Packing a little kit with spare pants, wipes and a bag means no worries.
[[CHILD]] can be in charge of the sticker chart.
